title: Google Cloud outage: Revolut suffers service disruption as bank customers report problems – business live
text:
Newsflash: Google’s cloud computing services have been hit by technical problems in Europe.
Google reports that “multiple Google Cloud services are experiencing elevated errors and intermittent network failures in europe-west2 region”, and it does not currently have a work around.
Incident affecting BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, Google Cloud Dataflow, Google Cloud NetApp Volumes, Google Cloud Pub/Sub, Google Cloud Storage, Google Compute Engine, Google Kubernetes Engine, Looker (Google Cloud core), Managed Airflow, Managed Service for Apache Kafka, Persistent Disk, Storage Transfer Service
Now, as then, it’s a reminder of the perils of relying on a small number of companies for operating the global internet, especially as more and more services have been moved onto the cloud.
Jake Moore, Global Cybersecurity Adviser at ESET, Europe’s leading cybersecurity company:
“Today’s outages highlight just how much dependence we put on a handful of technology giants to keep our digital lives running. With only a small number of major cloud providers to choose from, the knock-on effects can be catastrophic if something goes wrong and can leave millions of people unable to use everyday services.
“Cloud services are a huge point of failure and will always be a potential weakness in digital infrastructures. They could even become a potential target on such services by cybercriminals. Businesses therefore need to plan for when these services go down and have strict contingencies in place for this unfortunate inevitable event.”
Other companies affected by the Google Cloud outage include Royal Mail, DPD, BT, Cloudflare and Screwfix (on top of the companies we’ve already covered), according to tech news site The Register.
El Reg (as they’re affectionately known) adds:
Techies on Reddit said the interruption was having a cascading affect on multiple suppliers. One said: “oh man the classic one zone takes a nap and your non-HA service is in it.”
“Loads of stuff seems to be down, DNS somewhere,” mused another.
Halifax: some customers are having issues with our app and online
Halifax, which is part of LloydsBankingGroup, has confirmed some customers are having problems today.
Posting on X, Halifax says:
We’re aware some customers are having issues with our app and online. We’re sorry about this and are working hard to fix it. If you need to you can still call us. We’ll let you know as soon as it’s back to normal.
There are also reports that Rightmove has been affected by the Google Cloud outage.
Rightmove certainly uses Google Cloud for its new artificial intelligence services – including a new AI-powered Comparison Assistant launched earlier this month.
It has also been developing a AI-powered conversational property search “in close collaboration with Google Cloud”.
NewsThump, the satire and spoof news website, has been thumped by the Google Cloud outage – its site currently won’t load.
It says:
NewsThump has been down since 7am due to a major outage in the Google Cloud infrastructure (no, we don’t really understand that either). We have satirists chomping at the bit, and jokes to post as soon as everything comes back online...
“A person familiar with the matter” has told Reuters that Revolut’s service outage was related to the Google Cloud service disruption (as we speculated a little while ago…)
There are also some reports of problems with other UK financial services firms today – perhaps a sign that the Google Cloud outage is causing wider problems.
